title: No argument can part us from God’s love
source_text: Τολμῶ μὲν οὖν καί φημι ὅτι ἣν ἀξιοῖς ποιήσασθαι ἡμᾶς ἀπολογίαν ὑπεκλύει τὴν ἐν τοῖς πράγμασιν ἀπολογίαν καὶ τὴν ἐπιφανῆ τοῖς οὐκ ἀναισθήτοις δύναμιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. ὅμως δ᾿ ἵνα μὴ δοκῶμεν ὀκνεῖν πρὸς τὸ ἐπιταχθὲν ὑπὸ σοῦ, πεπειράμεθα ὑπαγορεῦσαι κατὰ τὴν παροῦσαν δύναμιν πρὸς ἕκαστον τῶν ὑπὸ Κέλσου γεγραμμένων τὸ φανὲν ἡμῖν ἀνατρεπτικὸν τῶν πιστὸν οὐδένα δυναμένων σεῖσαι λόγων αὐτοῦ. καὶ μὴ εἴη γε εὑρεθῆναί τινα τοιαύτην ἀνειληφότα ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ „ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ“, ὡς ὑπὸ τῶν ῥημάτων Κέλσου ἤ τινος τῶν ὁμοίων σεισθῆναι τὴν προαίρεσιν αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος μυρία ὅσα καταλέγων τὰ εἰωθότα χωρίζειν „ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ“ καὶ „ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ“, ὧν πάντων κρείττων ἦν ἡ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀγάπη. λόγον οὐ κατέταξεν ἐν τοῖς χωρίζουσι. πρόσχες γὰρ ὅτι πρότερον μέν φησι· „τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα; καθάπερ γέγραπται ὅτι ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα πᾶσαν τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς. ἀλλ᾿ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.“ δεύτερον δὲ ἄλλο τάγμα ἐκτιθέμενος τῶν πεφυκότων χωρίζειν τοὺς ἀνερματίστους ἐν θεοσεβείᾳ λέγει· „πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ. οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ, οὔτε ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα. οὔτε δυνάμεις οὔτε ὕψωμα, οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.“
pass_a_gloss: I dare (τολμάω) then and say that the defence (ἀπολογία) which you ask (ἀξιόω) us to make undoes/weakens (ὑπεκλύω) the defence in the facts (πράγματα) and the power (δύναμις) of Jesus manifest (ἐπιφανής) to those not without perception (ἀναίσθητος). Yet so that we may not seem to shrink (ὀκνέω) from what was enjoined (ἐπιτάσσω) by you, we have tried (πειράομαι) to dictate (ὑπαγορεύω) according to our present ability, toward each of the things written by Celsus, what appeared to us overturning (ἀνατρεπτικός) of his arguments (λόγοι), which are able to shake (σείω) no believer (πιστός). And may it not be (optative) that anyone be found who has taken up (ἀναλαμβάνω) such a love (ἀγάπη) of God 'in Christ Jesus' that his choice/resolve (προαίρεσις) be shaken by the words (ῥήματα) of Celsus or of one of the like. But Paul, listing (καταλέγω) countless (μυρία ὅσα) things wont to separate (χωρίζω) 'from the love of Christ' and 'love of God in Christ Jesus', than all of which the love in him was stronger, did not rank (κατατάσσω) argument/word (λόγος) among the things separating. For attend (προσέχω) that first he says: [Rom 8:35-37, incl. Ps 43(44):23: who will separate us from the love of Christ? affliction (θλῖψις), distress (στενοχωρία), persecution (διωγμός), famine (λιμός), nakedness (γυμνότης), danger (κίνδυνος), sword (μάχαιρα)? as written: for your sake we are put to death all the day, we were reckoned as sheep of slaughter (σφαγή); but in all these we more-than-conquer (ὑπερνικάω) through the one who loved us]. Second, setting out (ἐκτίθημι) another order (τάγμα) of things naturally apt (πέφυκα) to separate those unballasted (ἀνερμάτιστος) in godliness (θεοσέβεια), he says: [Rom 8:38-39: I am persuaded (πείθω, pf. pass.) that neither death nor life, nor angels (ἄγγελοι) nor principalities (ἀρχαί), nor things present (ἐνεστῶτα) nor things to come (μέλλοντα), nor powers (δυνάμεις), nor height (ὕψωμα), nor depth (βάθος), nor any other creature (κτίσις) will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord].
pass_b_english: I venture, then, to say that the defence you ask us to make weakens the defence that lies in the facts themselves, and the power of Jesus, which is plain to all who are not without perception. Still, so that we may not seem to shrink from the task you have laid on us, we have tried, as far as our present strength allows, to dictate in reply to each thing Celsus wrote whatever seemed to us to overturn his arguments, which can shake no believer. And may no one be found whose love of God “in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:39) is of such a kind that his resolve could be shaken by the words of Celsus or of anyone like him.

Paul lists a vast number of things that commonly separate people “from the love of Christ” (Romans 8:35) and from “the love of God in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:39), and the love within him was stronger than all of them; yet among the things that separate he did not set argument. For notice that he first says: “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword? As it is written, ‘For your sake we are being put to death all the day long; we were counted as sheep for the slaughter’ (Psalm 44:22). But in all these things we more than conquer through him who loved us” (Romans 8:35–37).

Second, setting out another order of things that by nature tend to separate those who have no ballast in godliness, he says: “For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 8:38–39).

choices.choice: LXX renumbering: Paul's quotation within Rom 8:36 is LXX Psalm 43:23 = English Psalm 44:22. Origen's text of Rom 8:36 reads 'πᾶσαν τὴν ἡμέραν' where the common text has 'ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν'; same sense. The point of the chapter turns on λόγος: Paul did not list 'argument' (λόγος) among the things that separate; rendered 'argument' to keep the link to Celsus's arguments (λόγων αὐτοῦ) earlier in the chapter. 'μὴ εἴη ... τοιαύτην ἀνειληφότα ἀγάπην ... ὡς ... σεισθῆναι' is rendered 'may no one be found whose love ... is of such a kind that his resolve could be shaken', keeping the result clause. 'ὑπεκλύει' (loosens, weakens) rendered 'weakens'. 'ἀνερματίστους' is a ship's word ('without ballast'); kept as an image because it is Origen's own. The edition's stray full stops inside the quotations ('ζωὴ.', 'ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα.') are ignored.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.

reviewer: claude (independent clause-by-clause pass against the Greek)

changes: 'dictate against each thing Celsus wrote what seemed' -> 'dictate in reply to each thing Celsus wrote whatever seemed' (stiff order)
'though they can shake no believer' -> 'which can shake no believer' (τῶν ... δυναμένων is attributive, not concessive)
'separate men' -> 'separate people' (no noun in the Greek); 'over all of them the love within him was stronger' -> 'the love within him was stronger than all of them' (ὧν πάντων κρείττων)
'Then, second' -> 'Second' (doubled); 'that by their nature separate' -> 'that by nature tend to separate' (πεφυκότων χωρίζειν)

Checked citations: Romans 8:35, 8:35-37, 8:38-39, 8:39 match; Paul's inner quotation is LXX Psalm 43:23 = English Psalm 44:22, correctly converted. 'The love within him' kept for Paul: ἦν (past) points to Paul's own love, though αὐτῷ could grammatically be Christ
open_items: Pref.3: 'ἡ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀγάπη' kept as Paul's own love ('the love within him'), because ἦν is past tense; αὐτῷ could grammatically refer to Christ. Not a blocker.

source_ref: Koetschau GCS 2 (1899), Contra Celsum, Preface 3, via the Perseus TEI
